prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1333; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision during a left turn at an intersection. Insured vehicle was struck by the other vehicle while turning, and the claimant has retained counsel who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on it, with coverage in force at the time of loss. No indication the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the accident occurred as described, and both place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time. The other driver gave the same account of the collision.

Entry 4: Scene photos reviewed. Damage to the vehicle is largely consistent with the impact described. A few old scratches are visible, which may predate this crash and will be noted for the appraiser.

Entry 5: Claimant reports shoulder pain following the impact. Injury is plausible for a collision of this type. Claimant has given the same account in each conversation so far.

Entry 6: Medical records show no prior injury to the same shoulder area on file. Treatment followed a typical course and has tapered as the claimant's condition improved.

Entry 7: Liability review in progress. Witness statements, photos, and the other driver's account all support the accident occurring as reported. File remains open pending final medical and appraisal review.
